quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.summary: Go from two folders to a checked scoreboard in 5 easy steps
quickStart.intro: JudgeDesk is a fast, safe, local offline programming contest judge. Prepare a problems folder and a contestants folder, then follow this simple 5-step workflow.

steps.loadProblems: Step 1 - Load problems: Choose «Load problems» on the toolbar and select the folder whose direct child directories represent contest problems.
steps.loadContestants: Step 2 - Load contestants: Choose «Load contestants» and select the folder whose direct child directories contain contestant submissions.
steps.configure: Step 3 - Configure problems: Open «Problem configuration» to review or adjust Input/Output modes (File I/O vs Standard I/O), Time/Memory limits, points, and checkers.
steps.judge: Step 4 - Grade submissions: Choose «Judge» on the toolbar. JudgeDesk compiles and executes only the checked contestant/problem intersections with real-time progress.
steps.save: Step 5 - Inspect & save: Double-click any score cell for test-by-test details. Save a .judgedesk contest archive or export the scoreboard to Excel (.xlsx).

quickStart.offlineNote: All instructions in this Help Center are packaged offline with JudgeDesk. Contest grading operates completely without an internet connection.

foldersReload.title: Folders, loading & Reload
foldersReload.summary: Contest directory structure and non-destructive reload
foldersReload.intro: Problems and contestant submissions are organized into two separate directory trees. You can select them using the folder dialogs or drag-and-drop folders directly into the app.

layout.problems: Problems root (Problems): One direct child folder per problem. The folder name serves as the problem code (e.g., BAI1, SUM, PRIME...).
layout.tests: Individual problem directory: Subdirectories for each test (Test01, Test02... or 1, 2...), containing input/output files (e.g., BAI1.INP/BAI1.OUT), Config.cfg, and optional custom checker source files.
layout.contestants: Contestants root (Contestants): One direct child folder per contestant. The folder name appears on the scoreboard (e.g., NguyenVanA, TranThiB, HS01...).
layout.submissions: Contestant submission files: Named following the pattern <ProblemCode>.<extension> (e.g., BAI1.cpp, BAI1.py, BAI1.pas, BAI1.c, BAI1.java). Filenames are case-insensitive.

foldersReload.reloadDescription: When contestants submit new files or test cases are updated, click «Reload» (or press F5) to rescan the directories without losing existing scores or problem configurations.
foldersReload.selectionNote: Reload preserves all your existing checked/unchecked selections. Newly discovered problems and contestants start checked by default so you can grade them immediately.

problemCheckers.title: Problem & checker configuration
problemCheckers.summary: Input/output, limits, points, groups, and checkers
problemCheckers.intro: Right-click a problem column or open its action menu and choose «Problem configuration». Settings belong specifically to that problem and are saved to its Config.cfg file.

items.io: Input/Output mode: Choose Standard I/O (cin/cout, stdin/stdout) or File I/O (specify exact .INP and .OUT filenames).
items.limits: Resource limits: Configure Time Limit (milliseconds) and Memory Limit (megabytes). Test-specific limits can override problem defaults where needed.
items.points: Scoring method: Supports per-test scoring or grouped scoring (Subtasks - requiring all tests in a group to pass to receive points).
items.checkers: Built-in checkers: Word-by-word (ignores extra whitespace and trailing newlines, most common), Line-by-line, Exact binary, or Floating-point (with customizable tolerance).
items.customCheckers: Custom checkers: Supports custom checkers written in C++ (using standard testlib.h or Themis argument signatures) or Python (.py). Place the checker source directly in the problem directory.

problemCheckers.configFileNote: Saving writes problem settings to Config.cfg inside the problem directory, making contest problem packages completely portable.
problemCheckers.resultWarning: Changing settings that affect judging (such as I/O mode, checker, or points) invalidates previous scores. JudgeDesk asks for confirmation and clears that problem's old scores/logs when saved.

judgingResults.title: Judging & results
judgingResults.summary: Selections, verdicts, details, regrading, and export
judgingResults.intro: JudgeDesk grades checked rows and columns inside a secure native sandbox, strictly enforcing execution limits.

items.selection: Grading scope: Use checkboxes in the contestant column and problem headers to grade all or specific subsets of submissions.
items.progress: Judging progress: Displays active contestant, problem, testcase progress, and verdicts in real-time. Click «Stop» to cancel safely.
items.details: Inspect details: Double-click any scored cell to inspect compilation status, individual test verdicts, execution time, memory usage, score, and checker feedback.
items.actions: Context menu actions: Right-click rows, columns, or cells to regrade, view details, or clear results.
items.export: Export to Excel: Export selected contestants and problems to a standardized Excel (.xlsx) workbook with full score summaries and metadata.
items.archive: Contest archive (.judgedesk): Package problems, submissions, configuration, and judging results into a single file for archival or sharing.

judgingResults.verdicts:
• AC (Accepted): Solution produced the exact expected output.
• WA (Wrong Answer): Output differed from expected answer.
• CE (Compilation Error): Code failed to compile (double-click cell to inspect compiler logs).
• RE (Runtime Error): Program crashed or exited abnormally (segmentation fault, division by zero, stack overflow).
• TLE (Time Limit Exceeded): Program exceeded time limit.
• MLE (Memory Limit Exceeded): Program exceeded memory limit.
• OLE (Output Limit Exceeded): Program produced excessive output.
• PE (Presentation Error): Output formatting error (extra spaces/newlines).
• JE (Judge Error): Environment or execution engine error.
• PARTIAL: Partial score granted by custom checker.
judgingResults.archivePrivacy: A .judgedesk archive is a ZIP-compatible container. Protect it carefully if the contest contains confidential test cases or unpublished problems.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts & Navigation
shortcuts.summary: Themis-compatible shortcuts and full mouse-free keyboard navigation
shortcuts.intro: JudgeDesk provides a full set of keyboard shortcuts matching traditional Themis, allowing rapid operation and full scoreboard navigation without a mouse.
shortcuts.macNote: On macOS, the Ctrl key is automatically mapped to Command (⌘). For example, ⌘N to create a new contest, ⌘S to save, and ⇧⌘S for Save As.

f5.description: Reload problems and contestants from disk, preserving active checkbox selections.

f9.description: Start judging (or continue judging un-scored problems).

f12.description: Export scoreboard results to an Excel (.xlsx) file.

ctrlShiftS.description: Save current contest under a new file name (Save As...).

ctrlShiftI.description: Toggle selection of the currently focused problem.

esc.description: Immediately close any open modal, dialog, or popover menu.

arrows.description: Navigate focus between contestant rows and problem columns on the scoreboard.

space.description: Toggle checkbox of the currently focused contestant or problem.

enter.description: Open testcase details window when focused on a scored cell.

toolchains.title: Languages & toolchains
toolchains.summary: Core, Full, statuses, paths, and quick troubleshooting
toolchains.intro: The compiler/runtime source answers where a language comes from. Readiness answers what JudgeDesk is currently allowed to do with it. These are separate facts.

full.description: Includes supported managed packages and selects them automatically on first launch. Choose Full during an update to replace bundled packages with those from the new release. On macOS, bundled packages cover Python, Pascal, and Java; C/C++ still requires Apple Clang and the macOS SDK from Xcode Command Line Tools.

core.description: Does not bundle every compiler/runtime. It probes PATH first, then a bounded list of standard locations, and shows the detected version and executable path. Choosing Core during an update preserves the selected compiler sources and paths.

detected.description: A supported executable answered a quick version/path probe. Detection alone does not promise submission execution.

ready.description: JudgeDesk can compile or run contestant submissions with the active execution protection for this language.

checker.description: The installation can support checker work but is not approved for contestant submissions in the current mode.

missing.description: No usable executable was found. Choose a path, install/apply a managed package, then scan again.

strict.description: A local toolchain becomes submission ready only after its strict probe passes. Submissions then retain the full sandbox, including filesystem and network isolation.

resourceOnly.description: Allows a local toolchain that cannot use the full sandbox to run with resource controls. JudgeDesk still enforces TLE, MLE, and process-tree cleanup, but does NOT isolate the filesystem or network.

toolchains.localCompatibilityWarning: Enable this only if you accept that contestant source may read or write files available to the teacher account and may access the network. A managed Full package remains the safer choice.
toolchains.troubleshootingTitle: If a language is not ready

troubleshooting.rescan: Open the compiler & runtime manager and scan again after changing PATH or installing a compiler.
troubleshooting.path: Confirm the displayed executable is the intended compiler/runtime, especially when several versions are installed.
troubleshooting.version: Run the same executable's version command in a terminal. Remove broken PATH entries or choose the correct local path.
troubleshooting.managed: In Full, prefer the package included with JudgeDesk. For C/C++ on macOS, install Xcode Command Line Tools if Apple Clang is not detected. In Core, apply a managed package when local execution is not compatible with native protection.
troubleshooting.restart: If the installer changed system environment variables, close and reopen JudgeDesk so the desktop process receives the new PATH.

toolchains.integrityNote: Local detection is intentionally a fast version/path probe, not a full integrity scan. Managed package signatures and hashes are checked during download/extraction instead of on every app start.

compileFlags.title: Per-problem compile flags
compileFlags.summary: Presets, custom arguments, Config.cfg, and score invalidation
compileFlags.intro: Compile flags are selected in Problem configuration for each problem. They are stored with that problem in Config.cfg; they are not a global toolchain preference.
compileFlags.checkerNote: Changing the compile profile does not change the problem checker. The checker and compile configuration are independent fields in the same Config.cfg.

themis.description: Default for older Config.cfg files without compile metadata. Keeps the established C++14/C11 behavior for reproducible regrading.

modern.description: C++ uses GNU++20 with -O2 -pipe; C uses GNU17 with -O2 -pipe. Select it explicitly for a contest that permits these standards.

icpc.description: C++ uses GNU++20 with -O2 -g; C uses GNU11 with -O2 -g, following the referenced World Finals configuration.

custom.description: Enter additional arguments for this problem. JudgeDesk previews parsed arguments and rejects source/output/toolchain/plugin overrides that could escape the managed command.

compileFlags.platformNote: Config.cfg stores platform-independent arguments. JudgeDesk adds required output, Windows stack/static-link, or macOS compatibility arguments for the active compiler; it does not apply Windows-only flags to Apple Clang.
compileFlags.invalidationWarning: Changing a problem's profile or effective flags changes the compiled program. Saving the change requires confirmation and deletes that problem's old scores/logs before the next grading run.
compileFlags.restore: To return to established behavior, choose Themis compatibility in that problem and save. Updating JudgeDesk does not silently rewrite a profile already stored in Config.cfg.

portable.title: Portable compatibility
portable.summary: What the current release supports and what remains future work
portable.notShipped: JudgeDesk does not ship or support a portable application archive. The supported release artifacts remain the Windows installer and macOS disk image.
portable.compatibility: The application is being kept compatible with a future extract-and-run package, but signing, updater behavior, writable data location, WebView/runtime dependencies, and clean-machine testing must be solved before release.

items.installer: Use the official installer or disk image and verify its published checksum.
items.contestArchive: The .judgedesk contest format is portable between supported Windows and macOS installations; this does not make the application itself portable.
items.futureWindows: A future Windows option would use a verified ZIP, not an old-style self-extracting executable.
items.futureMac: A future macOS option must preserve the signed app bundle, executable permissions, and Gatekeeper behavior.

portable.terminology: Install-free and true portable are different: true portable would also keep data/logs beside the app. No such mode is enabled in this release.

about.title: About JudgeDesk
about.summary: Version, edition, build identity, paths, and diagnostics
about.intro: JudgeDesk is a local Vietnamese programming-contest desktop judge for Windows and Apple Silicon macOS. It keeps contest preparation, grading, detailed results, archives, and exports in one desktop workflow.
about.themisCredit: JudgeDesk's offline, teacher-first workflow and contextual help are inspired by Themis. This Help Center is newly written for JudgeDesk and does not copy Themis text, screenshots, or assets.
about.disclaimer: JudgeDesk is an independent product. It is not Themis, is not affiliated with the Themis authors, and does not claim endorsement or sponsorship by Vietnam's Ministry of Education and Training.
